definition: AI Overviews is an artificial intelligence (AI) feature integrated into Google Search that produces AI-generated responses at the top of search results.
details: It uses the Gemini 3 family of large language models developed by Google DeepMind. It launched in May 2024 in the United States, and globally by October 2024. A June 2025 study found its most cited sources as Quora, followed by Reddit. The feature has been criticized for its inaccuracy, hallucination, reducing web traffic and not being able to be opted out.

explainer.lead: AI Overviews puts a generated answer above Google Search results, with links to web sources. It can make information quicker to scan, but its mistakes and its tendency to keep users on the results page have raised concerns about accuracy, publisher traffic, and competition.

tiers.eli5: Imagine asking a librarian a question and getting a short note before you see the bookshelf. The note is written by a computer after reading web pages, and it includes links so you can check them. Sometimes the note is wrong or makes things up, so it should not be trusted just because it appears first.
tiers.practitioner: AI Overviews is applied within Google Search, where Gemini-family language models turn web content into concise summaries with source links and adjustable language complexity. For publishers, prominent summaries can reduce visits even when a page ranks highly, and one cited Pew study found that only 1% of users clicked the supplied source links. Generated statements can be inaccurate, nonsensical, or hallucinated, so links do not eliminate the need for validation.
tiers.paperLevel: In plain-text notation, AI_Overview(q) = LLM_summary(web content relevant to query q), rendered above conventional search results together with source links. The feature originated in Google's Search Generative Experience, unveiled at Google I/O in May 2023, and was rebranded as AI Overviews at Google I/O in May 2024. Known limits include factual errors, nonsensical or harmful outputs, hallucinations about nonexistent idioms, and reduced incentives to visit source websites.

explainer.example: In May 2024, an AI Overview suggested applying glue to pizza, while another suggested eating rocks; Google temporarily restricted the tool after such nonsensical and harmful suggestions, illustrating why generated answers still need checking.

usedIn.detail: Displays generated summaries and source links above search results.

usedIn.name: Search Generative Experience
usedIn.detail: The Google experiment in which the feature was first introduced in May 2023.

explainer.intuition: Instead of making you assemble an answer from several result snippets, Search tries to write the short answer for you. The linked pages remain important because the generated text is not guaranteed to be correct.
howItWorks: A user enters a search query.
The system uses web content related to the queried topic.
A Gemini-family language model generates a concise summary.
The summary and links to sources appear above search results.
Users can choose simplified or more detailed language.
explainer.whyItMatters: AI Overviews changes search from mainly pointing to pages into also making new statements about their content. That affects what users believe, whether publishers receive visits, and how responsibility is assigned when an answer causes harm.
misconceptions: It is not merely a collection of quoted snippets: it generates a new summary from web content.
Including source links does not guarantee that every generated statement is accurate.
It is not simply a feature users can opt out of whenever they prefer ordinary results.
